correctness.rationale: On a cycle a pair monitors precisely the edges of its unique shorter arc (none if antipodal). An arc between probes that crosses an edge of an unprobed gap must traverse the entire gap, so a gap of at least n/2 prevents monitoring. Conversely all shorter gaps are monitored by their own endpoints. The empty set and singletons cannot monitor, and the short-gap bound excludes pairs. Rooting a labeled subset at any of its m probes gives the factor n/m. Deleting a probe merges two adjacent gaps. Summing the lower bounds on those merged lengths gives m(h+1)≤2n, hence only triples for odd n and at most four probes for even n. Equality in the even four-probe case forces alternating gaps and hence the antipodal pairs. For a triple there cannot be two oversized gaps: 2(h+1)≥n and the third gap is positive. This corrects the harmless strict-inequality slip in Lemma 5 for even n. The claimed counts and the cases n=3,4 follow. An independent bounded edge-deletion distance check through n=9 matched both enumerations, but is not the proof.
residual_risks: The review relies on the symbolic derivation, not on extending the independent finite check to the frozen verifier's full range.
